Q: Career Advice: Mastering C/AUTOSAR/Yocto vs. Expanding to Physical AI/ROS? A:

Stack Overflow works best when you ask one question at a time. That allows people to write focused answers and makes it easier for future askers with a similar question to quicjkly tell if your question will be helpful to them. Stack Overflow is first and foremost a library, so if your question isn't going to be useful to others, it's not useful enough to keep.

Also note that we have no idea who you are and know nothing about you. We don't know how well you can retain and apply knowledge and how well you can combine existing knowledge to solve new problems, so it's next to impossible to make good suggestions on what courses or career trajectory you should take. At best you'll get answers dealing in generalities.

Here's a generality: A junior programmer isn't expected to know everything; they are expected to know barely anything. Schools don't have the time to go particularly deep in anything unless you're specializing, and most things worth specializing in you don't get particularly good at without a lot of practice. We'll hire a junior programmer in hopes that you're good at something in 3-5 years and enjoyed working with us, and on the cool projects we do, enough to not go somewhere else when you are good. In the meantime you get an escalating series of tasks that are useful to us and a more-or-less proportionally lower oversight. If after a code review or a round of testing and profiling you're asked to speed things up N% or try replacing a chunk of the logic with Hoosamadinkle's Algorithm instead of the reviewer making the changes themselves, you're moving up, baby.

Q: ERROR [42000] [IBM] [System I Access ODBC Driver] [DB2 for i5/OS]SQL0104 Token _ was not valid A:

This is IBM Db2 Syntax for ADD_DAYS function. See this link for details.

select DDMAST."ACCTNO" from DAT589.DDMAST where DATOP7 = (TO_CHAR(ADD_DAYS(CURRENT_DATE, -1), 'yyyyDDD'))

Might want to try this instead.

select DDMAST."ACCTNO" from DAT589.DDMAST where DATOP7 = (TO_CHAR(CURRENT_DATE - 1 DAY, 'yyyyDDD'))
